standard_prerequisites.use: Is the property being compared and the lemma that reduces it to the polynomial presentation.

standard_prerequisites.name: Finiteness of an algebra map giving monic equations for a generating set
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the monic polynomials that present B as a quotient of a polynomial extension.

core_obligations: Choose a surjection R[x_1, ..., x_n] -> A and elements y_1, ..., y_m of B generating B over A (proof lines 21369-21370).
Use finiteness of A -> B to find monic polynomials P_j(T) in R[x_1, ..., x_n][T] with P_j(y_j) = 0 in B (proof lines 21371-21373).

Assemble the displayed commutative diagram with corners R[x_1, ..., x_n, y_1, ..., y_m], its quotient by the P_j(y_j), the polynomial ring in the x's, and the algebras A and B (proof lines 21374-21382).

Observe that the top horizontal arrow and the top right vertical arrow satisfy the hypotheses of the finite-pushforward lemma, so that K^bullet is m-pseudo-coherent (respectively pseudo-coherent) as a complex of R[x_1, ..., x_n]-modules exactly when it is so as a complex of R[x_1, ..., x_n, y_1, ..., y_m]-modules (proof lines 21383-21389).
Conclude the stated equivalence for K^bullet as a complex of B-modules and as a complex of A-modules (statement conclusion).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring R, a finite map A -> B of finite type R-algebras, an integer m, and a complex K^bullet of B-modules, and asserts that K^bullet is m-pseudo-coherent (respectively pseudo-coherent) relative to R if and only if K^bullet viewed as a complex of A-modules is so (source lines 21359-21366). The proof reduces the comparison to a single polynomial presentation. It chooses a surjection R[x_1, ..., x_n] -> A and elements y_1, ..., y_m generating B over A; since A -> B is finite each y_i satisfies a monic equation over A, so one finds monic polynomials P_j(T) in R[x_1, ..., x_n][T] with P_j(y_j) = 0 in B (proof lines 21369-21373). These data assemble into the displayed commutative diagram whose corners are the polynomial rings in the x's and in the x's and y's, the quotient by the P_j(y_j), and the algebras A and B (proof lines 21374-21382). The substantive observation is that the top horizontal arrow and the top right vertical arrow of that diagram satisfy the hypotheses of the finite-pushforward lemma for pseudo-coherent complexes, so that K^bullet is m-pseudo-coherent (respectively pseudo-coherent) as a complex of R[x_1, ..., x_n]-modules exactly when it is so as a complex of R[x_1, ..., x_n, y_1, ..., y_m]-modules (proof lines 21383-21389). The two outer comparisons then give the stated equivalence. The non-routine content is the construction of the monic polynomials realising the finite algebra map as a quotient of a polynomial extension.
